text.title: Product Lifecycle Management Examples
text.summary: Worked end-to-end examples showing signals → stage tag → matched investment strategy → routed playbook for a representative product.

example.title: Solo SaaS at 18 months — Growth to Maturity transition
example.note: $5K MRR, 18 months live. Signups flat quarter on quarter, the cohort retention curve is flattening rather than decaying, margin is healthy. Three of four signals agree on maturity, so confidence is high and the acquisition playbook is retired in favour of retention.
example.code: { "product_id": "acme-saas-core", "as_of": "2026-05-23", "signals": { "yoy_growth": 0.08, "monthly_churn": 0.015, "nps": 42, "market_share": 0.18 }, "stage": "maturity", "stage_confidence": "high", "investment_strategy": "Retention + efficiency: invest in NPS-moving fixes and CAC reduction; freeze new-segment expansion.", "routed_playbook": "retention-and-efficiency", "transition_memo": "Growth->Maturity: YoY 30%->8%, churn stable, NPS plateau; redirect growth budget to retention.", "sunset_plan_link": null }

example.title: Vibes tag with no confidence and no routed playbook
example.note: Stage asserted from feel, one signal supplied, no confidence label, and the strategy paragraph names no playbook — so nothing downstream changes. Violates stage-classification-quantitative, stage-confidence-labelled and stage-routes-to-playbook.
